summary:
The biggest move this week was in Texas, where the state's environmental agency issued an air permit on Nov. 16 for SpaceX's 750 MW off-grid gas plant at Starbase, three weeks before Gov. Abbott's data center permit pause was due to lift and while ERCOT's audit of large loads is still unfinished. Its nitrogen-oxide cap sits just under the level that would trigger a public hearing. SpaceX was also revealed as the company behind a 6 GW, $50 billion campus in Cochise County, Arizona, one of the largest proposals on this map; its zoning hearing is Dec. 9.

The pattern is the same across the new entries: build your own gas plant and stay off the shared grid. Microsoft's 2.67 GW Chevron-powered Pecos campus and a 1-3 GW gas-fired site on Alaska's North Slope, which won a 50-year state lease, join the tracker. Mississippi upheld the permit for SpaceXAI's 41 turbines in Southaven.

Elsewhere, momentum slowed. Project Jupiter's air-permit decision, due Nov. 23, was put off with no new date, so New Mexico's largest campus still has no approved power. Loudoun County, Virginia, the country's largest data center market, voted 7-1-1 on Nov. 17 to pause some new data center and substation applications. Fermi swapped its collapsed TensorWave lease for a 600 MW deal with an unnamed hyperscaler, but no lease is signed.

For household bills: off-grid plants keep their costs off utility rates but add local air pollution and gas demand. The fights that decide who pays, including Louisiana's December vote on Meta's seven gas plants and the Senate's data center cost bill, are still unresolved.

projects.name: Stargate Abilene
projects.power: On-site natural gas plus grid power, including local wind (per Epoch AI)
projects.cost: not reported in the sources cited
projects.note: Partly operating: Epoch AI estimated four of eight buildings running in April, with completion projected for Q4 2026. A planned expansion toward 2 GW was dropped in March (see separate entry).

projects.name: Abilene Stargate expansion
projects.company: Crusoe (developer); Oracle and OpenAI (dropped); Meta reported in talks
projects.power: Not settled; DCD, citing The Information, reported power would not be ready at the site for about a year
projects.note: Oracle and OpenAI dropped plans to take the site from 1.2 GW to 2 GW (about 800 MW more); Nvidia reportedly paid Crusoe a $150 million deposit and courted Meta for the capacity, with no deal reported signed. A Stacker piece this week cited it as an example of the delays now hitting about half of planned capacity.

projects.name: Frontier campus (Stargate)
projects.company: Vantage Data Centers; part of the OpenAI/Oracle Stargate program
projects.power: On-site natural gas microgrid
projects.note: Ten buildings planned; the first was expected online in the second half of 2026. Epoch AI put the Stargate share at 2 GW, above Vantage's 1.4 GW campus figure.

projects.name: Stargate Milam County
projects.power: SB Energy plans to build new generation and storage for most of the campus's power
projects.cost: not reported in the sources cited
projects.note: Steel framing and roofing visible on the first building in April; projected completion Q4 2028 per Epoch AI.

sources.title: OpenAI Stargate: where the US sites stand

projects.name: Project Jupiter (Stargate New Mexico)
projects.power: Natural gas microgrids with Bloom Energy fuel cells and batteries; El Paso Electric backup service was proposed and withdrawn
projects.cost: $165 billion expected investment over the industrial revenue bond's life (as reported)
projects.note: The developer waived the Nov. 23 deadline for a state decision on the gas microgrid's air permit, and on Nov. 3 it and the state asked to cancel the Dec. 7 hearing until regulators finish reviewing October revisions; no new date is set, so the campus still has no approved power. The county sent a second breach notice Nov. 10; the microgrid is reported at up to 2.45 GW, above the 2.2 GW used here.

projects.power: DTE Energy supplies 100% under a contract approved by Michigan regulators, plus a project-financed battery system
projects.cost: not reported in the sources cited
projects.note: Foundation work under way in April; projected completion Q4 2028 per Epoch AI.

projects.name: Lighthouse campus (Stargate Wisconsin)
projects.company: Vantage Data Centers; OpenAI and Oracle
projects.power: We Energies; Oracle would pay for 125 to 250 MW from the Point Beach nuclear plant under an extended NextEra contract
projects.note: Oracle's Oct. 2 offer to buy Point Beach power, which it says would save We Energies customers about $300 million in fuel costs over 2027-2033, awaits Wisconsin PSC approval; data centers are now a bipartisan campaign issue in the state.

projects.name: Hyperion
projects.power: Entergy Louisiana: three gas units approved in 2025 and seven more proposed, for ten in all (754 MW each, about 7.5 GW as reported), with batteries and transmission
projects.cost: Entergy's estimates for the new generation are reported at $12.9 billion and about $13.6 billion; Meta's regional investment over $50 billion (as reported)
projects.note: Entergy has also gone to court to expropriate easements from 14 Lincoln Parish landowners for a 58-mile, 500 kV line to the campus, arguing it serves the public. The Nov. 9 landowner suit against the PSC's fast track for the seven gas plants is pending; Entergy still plans to seek approval in December (Dec. 10 per KRVS). The Lens reports about $3.4 billion of the generation cost would fall to other customers after Meta's 20-year contract.

projects.name: Prometheus
projects.power: Grid (AEP Ohio area); Meta's disclosure this week did not detail the power mix
projects.note: Meta said the first phase is live, with hundreds of thousands of GPUs and a plan to scale to about a gigawatt and roughly a million GPUs; 1,000 MW is the planned scale, not current draw.

sources.title: Meta details Ohio Prometheus data center campus, with first phase live

projects.name: Colossus 2 and Southaven sites
projects.power: On-site gas turbines in Southaven (41 permanent turbines permitted in March to replace 27 unpermitted ones) and Tesla Megapacks
projects.cost: more than $20 billion for the Mississippi facility (as reported)
projects.note: At the close of a Nov. 9-10 hearing Mississippi's permit board voted 6-1 to uphold the permit for 41 permanent gas turbines at Southaven, rejecting community groups' appeal; they can still go to court, and the NAACP's federal Clean Air Act suit continues. The 2 GW figure is Musk's total for Colossus training compute, not a utility-filed load.

projects.name: Homer City Energy Campus
projects.company: Homer City Redevelopment with Kiewit; Amazon Web Services (tenant)
projects.power: A 4.5 GW natural gas plant on the former coal plant site
projects.note: Indiana County's planning commission accepted (not approved) AWS's application for 36 buildings on 1,100 acres on Oct. 14, starting a 90-day review that runs to Jan. 12; a state wastewater permit for cooling-tower discharge is separate. 4,500 MW is the gas plant's size; a campus load hasn't been reported.

projects.name: Susquehanna campus
projects.power: Up to 1,920 MW from Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant under a 17-year PPA, moving from behind-the-meter to grid-connected retail service
projects.note: Deliveries ramp to 840-1,200 MW by 2029 and the full 1,920 MW by 2032; the original 300 MW behind-the-meter setup was to be reconfigured during a spring 2026 refueling outage.

sources.title: Talen, Amazon Launch $18B Nuclear PPA—A Grid-Connected IPP Model for the Data Center Era

projects.name: Project Rainier
projects.power: Indiana Michigan Power (AEP) for Phase I; NIPSCO for Phase II
projects.cost: $11 billion Phase I plus $15 billion Phase II (as reported)
projects.note: Phase I has run since October 2025 and Phase II was slated to start in 2026; the profile cited gives conflicting counts of buildings live.

projects.name: Fairwater
projects.power: We Energies
projects.cost: $4.7 billion of Wisconsin construction spending 2024-2028 (as reported)
projects.note: The first building went live in June, a second is due in 2028 and 15 more were approved in January. Microsoft hasn't published a load; 450 MW is a tracker site's estimate.

projects.name: Paducah AI campus (DOE site)
projects.company: Brookfield (developer); NextEra Energy (power); no tenant named
projects.power: NextEra-built generation of up to 2 GW of grid-connected gas and 2.6 GW of batteries; Big Rivers Electric wholesale, Jackson Purchase Energy retail
projects.note: Up to 1.8 GW of utility capacity for more than 1.2 GW of compute on the former uranium enrichment plant. Incumbent judge-executive Craig Clymer, who campaigned on the site's investment, won a third term Nov. 3 over George Bray, 12,077 to 7,558 (unofficial).

projects.name: Project Matador (HyperGrid)
projects.company: Fermi America with Texas Tech University System; an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler (lease under negotiation)
projects.power: Mostly behind the meter: gas turbines first, with four AP1000 reactors under NRC review, plus solar, wind, batteries and grid power
projects.cost: not reported; the hyperscaler agreed to a $200 million prepayment (as reported)
projects.note: On Nov. 12 Fermi said an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler agreed to an initial 600 MW with development starting in 2027 and a $200 million prepayment, though a definitive lease is still being negotiated; the TensorWave lease and AMD credit support were terminated. Fermi cites 2.2 GW of current capacity and targets of 11 GW to about 17 GW, all subject to customers, permits and financing.

projects.name: Project Jade
projects.company: Google (bought the project from Crusoe); Black Hills Corp. (power)
projects.power: Black Hills: up to 590 MW of grid service (564 MW of new gas at Cheyenne Prairie plus 26 MW of market power), and management of about 2.1 GW of third-party resources through a private microgrid; total resource mix about 2.7 GW
projects.cost: Google plans to invest $17 billion; $1.8 billion for Black Hills' new gas generation (as reported)
projects.note: Crusoe confirmed on Nov. 6 that it sold the unfinished southeastern Wyoming project to Google for an undisclosed price, and Google says it will invest $17 billion in the campus; Crusoe had once talked of scaling it to 10 GW. Black Hills' agreements through 2048 call for service from late 2027 and peak load in 2030, with four approvals still pending.

projects.name: Alton Steel site campus
projects.power: Grid-connected through Ameren Illinois, with TerraWatt paying for local upgrades
projects.note: New this week: up to 1 GW in 200 MW blocks on a former steel mill, contingent on rezoning and an Ameren study; first block late 2027 to early 2029 and no tenant signed.

sources.title: Gigawatt-scale data center proposed for steel mill in Illinois

projects.name: Taylor Technology Campus
projects.company: Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers
projects.power: 500 MW under the city agreement with an option for 500 MW more; natural gas available for behind-the-meter generation
projects.note: Taylor's council unanimously approved an economic development agreement this month; construction 2027-2029 with first power in the first half of 2028.

sources.title: 1 GW Data Center Project Advances Near Austin

projects.name: El Paso data center
projects.power: El Paso Electric via McCloud Generation, 366 MW of modular gas units next to the site paid for by Meta, as a five-year bridge from 2027
projects.note: Meta's request grew from 220 MW to over 440 MW by 2027 and possibly 1 GW by 2029; 1,000 MW is that upper figure, and the plant stays off EPE's transmission system with long-term cost recovery left for later.

sources.title: Meta funds El Paso nat gas plant as interim power fix

projects.name: Project Cannoli
projects.power: DTE Electric under contracts approved by the Michigan PSC on Oct. 1; Google to fund up to 1,600 MW of renewables and 480 MW of batteries; DTE has also proposed about 2.1 GW of new gas in Milan and Handy townships
projects.cost: not reported; DTE's proposed gas plants estimated at $6.4 billion combined (as reported)
projects.note: The township planning commission gave final site-plan approval in mid-October; service is due in December 2027 with full load by December 2028. Regulators haven't ruled on DTE's proposed gas plants, and the PSC meets again Nov. 5.

sources.title: Google data center wins final approval in Wayne County: What residents need to know

projects.name: GW Ranch
projects.company: Pacifico Energy (developer); Amazon (owner of the data center buildings)
projects.power: Off-grid at first: up to 7.65 GW of on-site gas turbines (35 units), up to 750 MW of solar and 1.8 GW of batteries, designed to connect to the grid later
projects.cost: about $12 billion per the developer's February estimate (as reported)
projects.note: 7,650 MW is the on-site gas plant's size; a data center load hasn't been reported. Amazon filed permits in August for three 189,000-square-foot buildings after the state permitted the turbines in January; because it runs off the grid, its cost doesn't land on ERCOT customers' bills.

sources.title: Amazon Discloses Ownership of GW Ranch, Giant Texas Data Center-Gas Power Complex

projects.name: Project Camellia
projects.power: Georgia Power, under a 25-year agreement for 3.2 GW delivered over about four years; OpenAI says it pays for the electrical infrastructure
projects.note: On Nov. 6 three Effingham County residents sued OpenAI, its local entity, county commissioners and the development authority in state court, alleging concealment and a Georgia RICO violation over how the deal was made. OpenAI's Nov. 2 non-binding pledge to make up to 1,000 MW available for curtailment in grid emergencies is still being worked out with Georgia Power.

sources.title: Effingham County residents file damages lawsuit against OpenAI, county officials over Project Camellia
OpenAI Launches Grid Protectors Program With 1 GW Georgia Pledge

projects.name: Cochise County AI campus (SpaceX)
projects.power: Built beside the roughly 1 GW Apache Generating Station, which SpaceX says it could expand to more than 6 GW, with a 24 GWh battery system; AEPCO wholesale and SSVEC retail service; the application includes about $3.6 billion in grid upgrades
projects.note: SpaceX was revealed as the developer at a Nov. 4 town hall; it plans four phases of about 1.5 GW each on 747 acres, part of a $74 billion plan with Starbase. Written comments are due Nov. 27 and the county zoning hearing is Dec. 9; the Apache station had been slated to retire by 2028.

sources.title: SpaceX hid behind another name in the Arizona desert, and now it's going big
Largest data center proposal in Arizona heads to Cochise County. 1st community meeting scheduled

projects.name: Stratos Project
projects.company: Kevin O'Leary's Stratos (developer); no tenant named
projects.power: Off-grid natural gas behind the meter (turbines, with reciprocating engines for backup), fed by the Ruby Pipeline; models not yet selected
projects.note: An NRDC-commissioned study (not peer-reviewed) estimates the gas power could cause 5 to 45 premature deaths a year and up to $690 million in health costs; Stratos disputes it. Box Elder County approved the plan in May, but air permits are ahead; recent water filings describe 7.5 GW and first-phase permits are capped at 1 GW.

sources.title: Study projects health impacts from proposed data center; O'Leary's team disputes findings
Kevin O'Leary's colossal Utah data center hits a wall
Box Elder County approved the largest data center in the country. Now what?

projects.name: Starbase super-compute facility and gas plant
projects.power: An off-grid gas-fired plant: Texas's environmental agency issued the air permit for 35 turbines (about 750 MW) on Nov. 16; the original filing lists eight permanent turbines (about 708 MW) as the alternative; an affiliate's 8-mile gas pipeline is due in January 2027
projects.cost: $24 billion for the initial phases (as reported)
projects.note: Texas's environmental agency issued the plant's air permit on Nov. 16, before the governor's data center permit pause was due to lift on Dec. 10, with a nitrogen-oxide cap of about 248 tons a year, just under the 250-ton line that triggers a public hearing. The city's tax abatement vote is still set for Dec. 9; 748 MW is the turbines' capacity, as no data center load has been disclosed.

sources.title: Texas issues air permit for massive SpaceX data center
SpaceX Plans $74B Data Centers; Starbase Gas Plant Nitrogen Oxide Cap 1.14 Tons Under Federal Line
SpaceX Wants a Tax Break for a $24 Billion Gas Plant and Supercomputer at Starbase

projects.name: Sutton data center campus
projects.company: The Kraft Group and United Global Packaging Group
projects.power: Developers say they are in talks with ISO New England for grid power and are exploring treated wastewater for cooling; under a September state executive order they must bring their own energy or pay a fee
projects.note: New this week: a tentative plan for about 900 MW in 10 buildings, with the first two opening in 2029 and two more a year through 2033; no application has been filed. Massachusetts paused data center tax breaks in June and now requires community benefit agreements.

sources.title: 900-megawatt data center campus proposed for central Massachusetts, backed by Kraft Group
Kraft Group proposes $16B data center complex in Sutton

projects.name: Project Kilby (Microsoft Pecos campus)
projects.company: Microsoft; power from a Chevron subsidiary
projects.power: A co-located Chevron natural gas plant serving the campus behind the meter under a 20-year power-purchase agreement signed in June; Microsoft says it funds the generation
projects.note: Chevron says it is still working toward a final investment decision (expected by end-2026) with contracts, permits and financing unfinished, targeting first power in 2028 and full energization in 2031. 2,670 MW is the phased power project's size; Microsoft's data center capacity is put at about 2 GW, and Texas's data center permit pause could affect timing.

sources.title: Chevron says Project Kilby remains on schedule
Chevron to fuel massive Microsoft data center in Texas using natural gas

projects.name: STAK Energy Campus
projects.company: STAK Energy Corp.; tenant not reported
projects.place: Dalton Highway Milepost 390, North Slope (about 26 miles south of Deadhorse)
projects.power: Its own 1-3 GW natural gas plant burning North Slope gas (350-500 million cubic feet a day); not tied to the Railbelt grid, though it could sell power around Prudhoe Bay
projects.cost: about $500 million for initial site development (as reported)
projects.note: Alaska's natural resources commissioner signed a 50-year lease for 715 acres on Nov. 10; it still needs a federal wetlands permit and a state air permit and faces a 20-day reconsideration window. 3,000 MW is the top of the reported 1-3 GW generation range; no data center load has been given, and construction is expected to take six years.

sources.title: DNR approves STAK 50-year lease for 715.4 acres west of Dalton
Alaska approves 50-year land lease for large natural gas-powered data center in the Arctic

changes: Starbase (SpaceX): Texas issued the air permit for the 750 MW off-grid gas plant on Nov. 16, ahead of the governor's Dec. 10 pause date; status moved to permitted.
Cochise County, Ariz.: SpaceX revealed as the developer of the 6 GW, $50 billion campus; zoning hearing Dec. 9.
Colossus 2 (SpaceXAI): Mississippi's permit board voted 6-1 to uphold the 41-turbine Southaven permit.
Project Matador (Fermi): a 600 MW deal with an unnamed hyperscaler and a $200 million prepayment; TensorWave lease terminated.
Project Jupiter: the Nov. 23 air-permit deadline was waived and the Dec. 7 hearing pulled; no new date.
Project Camellia (OpenAI): residents filed a state-court RICO suit over the deal (Nov. 6).
Hyperion (Meta): Entergy sued Lincoln Parish landowners for easements for a 58-mile line to the campus.
Added: Microsoft's Pecos, Texas campus (Project Kilby), 2.67 GW of Chevron gas power; final investment decision pending.
